reason: Among the four, Claude at 200K tokens has by far the largest context and strongest reasoning; Titan Express, Command R (128K), and Nova Micro are smaller and force truncation/chunking.
Nova Micro is the lowest-cost, lowest-latency text-only Bedrock model, ideal for high-volume short-message intent classification; Opus/Sonnet/Llama 70B are larger and pricier.

Hierarchical chunking (parent/child) fits nested sections; child chunks give precision while parent context preserves relevance. Stem wording on which chunk reaches the LLM is loose but hierarchical is the only fit.
Semantic chunking splits on embedding-similarity meaning boundaries, keeping narrative ideas intact; smaller fixed, fixed-size hierarchical, and no-chunking all fail the topic-boundary requirement.

Cohere Embed Multilingual maps EN/FR/AR/JA into one shared vector space. Distractor is Titan MULTIMODAL (image+text), not the multilingual Titan Text V2, so it is correctly wrong; per-language indexes violate the single-model requirement.

Incremental data-source sync re-embeds only added/modified/deleted objects, minimizing cost/time; recreating the KB reprocesses all 2M, no-chunking does not limit scanned files, DynamoDB is not a valid document source.

Metadata filtering scopes retrieval to Finance docs from one index; per-department KBs add overhead, post-filtering leaks other data into the app, and Guardrails enforce content policy not document access.
Aurora PostgreSQL pgvector adds vector search inside the DB they already run, satisfying no-new-service; Pinecone/OpenSearch add systems and Neptune is a graph DB, not a vector store.
Redis Enterprise keeps vectors in memory for single-digit ms latency and reuses their caching platform; S3 Vectors is latency-tolerant, pgvector is disk-backed, Athena is interactive SQL.

Continued pre-training absorbs a large unlabeled corpus and domain vocabulary without labeled pairs; fine-tuning needs labeled data, RAG does not change internal language, few-shot cannot absorb a whole corpus.

Fine-tuning on thousands of labeled examples reliably enforces format/tone when knowledge is stable; RAG targets changing knowledge, continued pre-training needs unlabeled data, few-shot is less consistent and costlier.
Bedrock fine-tuning expects JSONL with one prompt/completion JSON object per line; CSV, a single JSON array, and raw text are not the accepted schema.

A customer managed KMS key gives the bank key-policy control, rotation, CloudTrail auditing, and revocation; service-owned keys are not customer-controlled, hardcoded keys are insecure, security groups are not encryption.

An interface VPC endpoint via PrivateLink keeps Bedrock API calls on the AWS network; NAT gateway still uses the public endpoint, you cannot front managed Bedrock with an ALB, IP whitelisting still uses the public path.

Verified: AWS geographic inference profiles (US/EU/APAC) route only within their geography, so an EU-scoped profile keeps data in EU; the other options falsely claim source-Region pinning, automatic residency, or fine-tuning as the control.

Bedrock is HIPAA-eligible under an AWS BAA and does not use inputs/outputs to train base models; it does not train on customer data, EC2 self-hosting is not required, and Guardrails alone do not establish HIPAA compliance.

Claude vision and Amazon Nova (Lite/Pro/Premier) multimodal models both accept image inputs and generate text; Titan Text Embeddings V2 only embeds, and Command Light and Titan Text Lite are text-only.

An interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) keeps API traffic on the AWS network and a customer managed KMS key encrypts data at rest; public+TLS, a public S3 bucket, and a wildcard permission are all insecure.

Metadata filtering and a document-matched chunking strategy both directly change what the retriever returns; output tokens, temperature, and swapping the generation model only affect generation, not retrieval.

Amazon does not train base models on inputs/outputs and Bedrock usage can be scoped to Regions for residency; invocation logging is optional, fine-tuning data is not shared with providers, and customer managed KMS keys are supported.
